lockup.summary: The company, its officers, directors and holders of nearly all its shares cannot sell for 180 days after the prospectus date. The co-founders and their related entities cannot sell for 270 days.

what: It makes Curodont, a peptide-based treatment that helps repair early tooth cavities and keep the natural tooth.
proceeds: The company expects about $154.5 million in net proceeds. It plans to use the money for general costs such as working capital, operating expenses and equipment. It may also buy other businesses, but has no deals agreed.
risks: The company's success depends on dentists and patients learning about and accepting its new Curodont cavity treatment.
Its results depend on distributors, especially Henry Schein, and on key customers such as Heartland.
Growing revenue depends on expanding its sales and marketing capabilities.
The company may have trouble managing its growth.
It relies on third-party manufacturers and suppliers to make and assemble its products.
